Alamance County by the numbers

What does the Alamance County Register of Deeds do for a home seller?

This is where the deed that passes title to your buyer gets recorded, and where the permanent index of deeds, deeds of trust, plats and easements for the whole county is kept. Staff here only record. Under North Carolina law they may not practice law, so they will not hand out legal forms or advise you on what a document does.

Graham is the seat and Burlington the largest community. Properties in Burlington, Mebane, Elon, Haw River and the rest of the county's thirteen townships all go through this one office.

The front counter keeps weekday hours of 8:00 to 5:00, but the last submission for recording is 4:30, a cutoff set when the county adopted G.S. 153A-94(b) in August 2013. The office phone menu has separate options for recording help, for earlier recorded documents, and for vital records.

What are the recording fees at the Alamance County Register of Deeds?

The published schedule below shows a deed at $26 through page 15, with $4 for every page after. A deed of trust is priced on a longer base. The deed of trust figure was reset effective October 1, 2016.

Recording and copy fees listed by the Alamance County Register of Deeds
ItemFee
Deed$26 for pages 1 to 15, then $4 per page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64 for pages 1 to 35, then $4 per page
Multiple documents in one filing$10 added to the recording fee
Non-standard document$25 added to the recording fee
Plat$21
Certified copy$5 for the first page, $2 per added page
Uncertified copy$0.25 per page

Vital record fees on the same schedule, such as marriage licenses and certified birth, death and marriage certificates, are cash or money order only. Ask the office which payment types it accepts for recording before you go.

How much is the North Carolina excise tax on a deed?

North Carolina taxes each conveyance at $1.00 per $500 of value, with a part-payment of $500 counted whole. The transferor pays it to the register of deeds ahead of recording, under G.S. 105-228.30. For a parcel in more than one county, payment goes where most of the value lies.

The register remits the proceeds to the county finance officer. One half stays with the county general fund, and the state receives the rest, after refunds and the county's collection allowance. Timber deeds are covered by the same statute.

You will not find this tax on the county's fee schedule, because it is a state levy, separate from the recording charge. Your settlement attorney reads the consideration off the deed and collects the tax alongside the fee. Ask to see the figure on your settlement statement before the closing date.

What formatting rules must a deed meet in Alamance County?

Paper deeds must satisfy G.S. 161-14(b), which the county restates on its recording page. A deed that fails still gets recorded, for an extra $25.

  • Sheets of 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Three blank inches above the first page text, with half an inch minimum elsewhere on page one and on all edges of later pages.
  • Black print on white paper, with nine point as the smallest legible font. Pen is allowed for blanks and corrections.
  • Printing on one side only.
  • The instrument's title at the top of page one, under the margin.

Plats follow a separate rule: mylar only, cut to 18 by 24 inches. Enclose a stamped self-addressed envelope sized for the recorded document.

What happens to the deed after it is recorded?

Staff stamp each instrument with the day and hour it arrived and record in arrival order. The statute gives the office up to 30 days to finish indexing. Keep the book and page number the county assigns, because it is how you will refer to the document later.

A step that surprises some sellers comes first. Deeds recorded since May 2, 2011 (timber deeds and releases excepted) pass through the county Tax Department for a delinquent tax certification. Overdue county tax stalls recording until it is paid, so request a payoff early.

Electronic recording has been available since November 2015 for everything but plats, so your attorney can submit through a vendor. After recording, Land Records at the Tax Department revises the owner name and mailing address. Straight sales move quicker than splits. Call with your book and page number if nothing changes after several weeks.

Which other Alamance County offices touch a house sale?

A sale here usually involves three offices besides this one, and each keeps a different slice of the record.

  • Tax Department, Land Records: at 124 W. Elm St. in Graham, phone (336) 228-1312. It owns the parcel's owner name, mailing address and tax map, and its staff want the book and page number of any recorded deed when you call about a change.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: holds estate filings and court orders, which establish who owns a house after a death or a court proceeding.
  • North Carolina Secretary of State: holds business filings. A merger, name change or dissolution alters how a company-owned parcel is listed.

Names on the county record follow the recorded deed letter for letter. A misspelling that appears on the deed itself needs a corrected document recorded here, and a lawyer can prepare it. A marriage or court-ordered name change does not alter the owner name unless a new document is recorded.

Tax bills are mailed in July and fall due September 1, so changing a mailing address before July keeps the bill from going astray after you sell.

How do I search or copy Alamance County land records?

Search recorded deeds by name through the office's online search, and go to the office itself for certified copies. The website cautions that online records are unofficial, and the paper records in the office are the official ones.

  • Certified copies: $5 for page one, $2 for each page after it.
  • Plain copies: $0.25 a page.
  • Owner, mailing address and legal description: the Tax Department's property record search.
  • Tax maps are drawn for assessment and are not surveys. Use a licensed surveyor and the recorded plat for any boundary question.

If you are paying off a mortgage, have the lender record the release, since cancellation of a deed of trust is itself a recorded instrument.

What local facts affect a deed transfer in Alamance County?

QuickFacts shows 83,187 housing units for July 2025 and 70,062 households in 2020 to 2024, at 2.44 people each. Nearly nine in ten residents (89.3%) lived at the same address a year before, and 28.7% of adults over 25 hold a bachelor's degree or better. With the July 2025 estimate of 186,177 running 8.6% over the April 2020 base, conveyances keep arriving.

The county dates to 1849, carved from Orange County, and takes its name from the creek where the Battle of Alamance was fought on May 16, 1771. When title runs through an estate, the Clerk of Superior Court files the estate papers and this office records the deeds the heirs or the court sign.

More questions about Alamance County, NC Register of Deeds

What is the last time of day to record a deed in Alamance County?

Documents must come in by 4:30 p.m. The doors stay open until 5:00, yet the recording cutoff arrives half an hour earlier under G.S. 153A-94(b).

Who pays North Carolina's deed excise tax?

The transferor does, ahead of recording. G.S. 105-228.30 sets $1.00 per $500 of value, rounding any part of $500 up.

What does it cost to record a deed here?

A deed costs $26 through page 15, then $4 per added page. Documents that miss the formatting rules carry a $25 surcharge.

Is electronic recording offered in Alamance County?

Yes, for every document except plats, since November 2015. Closing attorneys normally submit through a recording vendor.

Why did my deed have to go to the Tax Department first?

Deeds recorded after May 2, 2011, other than timber deeds and releases, need delinquent tax certification from the county Tax Department before recording. Unpaid county tax must be cleared first.

Where does Alleghany County record a deed?

A deed for Alleghany County land goes to the Register of Deeds, 348 South Main Street, Sparta, NC 28675. Call 336-372-4342 to reach the office. Staff are on site until 5:00 p.m., yet nothing is accepted for recording once the clock passes 4:30 p.m.

Alleghany sits in the Blue Ridge Mountains of northwestern North Carolina and was cut out of Ashe County by the 1858-1859 session of the legislature. The county seat is Sparta, and the same administration building that houses the register also holds the tax office. That matters for sellers, because a deed here cannot be recorded without a paper from the tax side of the building.

The register is a recording office. Staff explain county requirements and nothing more. Drafting and legal advice belong to your closing attorney. For ownership lookups by street address, the county points callers to its E-911 and Mapping office at 336-372-7920 instead of the register.

Which items does the Sparta office check on a deed?

The county's checklist asks for a notarized signature, a named drafter, the buyer's address, a tax certification, and payment of excise tax and fees.

  • The grantor's signature must be properly notarized.
  • Deeds and deeds of trust written in North Carolina must name the person who drafted them on the first page.
  • The grantee's address goes on the first page so the tax office knows where to send bills.
  • The tax certification from the Alleghany County tax administrator must be attached before recording.
  • The grantor pays the real estate excise tax when the deed is recorded.
  • Recording fees are paid before any document is accepted.

Page layout is checked as well. The county wants legal or letter size sheets, a roomy blank band across the top of page one, dark print no smaller than 10 points, one-sided pages, and the instrument title near the top. Pen is fine for blanks and corrections. A deed that falls short still gets recorded, with a $25.00 surcharge added to the normal charges.

Why does Alleghany County ask for a tax certification with every deed?

The county requires a tax certification form to accompany all deeds, and the register's FAQ repeats that a deed cannot be recorded without one. The tax office issues the form, and its phone number is 336-372-8291.

The certification rests on G.S. 105-361(a), which says the tax collector must furnish a written certificate on request showing the current and prior-year taxes, penalties, interest and costs that are a lien on a parcel. The county tax office FAQ goes further and says taxes on a parcel must be paid in full before a deed for it can be recorded. The request has to name the person in whose name the land was listed for each year. Request the form early, since an open bill can stall the recording.

In practice a seller should expect every county charge on the parcel, such as the solid waste fee and fire district tax, to be cleared at the table. Confirm whether your closing attorney or you will request the certificate.

What does recording a deed in Alleghany County cost?

A standard deed runs $26.00 through page 15 with $4.00 for every page beyond that, and the seller owes excise tax on top. The table gathers what the county prints and the statewide amounts it follows.

Alleghany County recording charges (county FAQ and checklist, G.S. 161-10)
ItemCharge as printed

Excise tax, paid by the grantor$2.00 for every $1,000 of price
Nonstandard document add-on$25.00

Certified copy$5.00 for page one, $2.00 per later page

Statute G.S. 105-228.30 states the same tax as one dollar per $500 or part of $500 and puts it on the seller. A mortgage-type document carries a higher base fee, which the lender's closing agent handles.

What do federal numbers show for Alleghany homes?

QuickFacts lists 11,479 people for July 2025, compared with 10,888 counted in 2020, across 234.84 square miles of land.

  • Housing units: 8,035 in 2025, against 5,177 households for 2020 to 2024.
  • Homeowners as a share of occupied homes: 74.4 percent.
  • Typical value of an owner's home: $214,800.
  • Median gross rent: $675.
  • People aged 65 or more: 31.4 percent.
  • Median household income: $47,172.

Housing units outnumber households by a wide margin, which fits a county with many second homes and seasonal cabins. The older age profile also means plenty of heirs end up selling a parent's house, and for those cases the deed from an estate has to meet the same recording rules described above.

How are Alleghany County property taxes set and when is the next revaluation?

The county tax rate printed for fiscal year 2026-27 is 0.597 per $100 of value, with a $108 residential solid waste fee and a fire district rate that depends on where the house sits. Real estate is reappraised at least every eight years, and Alleghany's last revaluation took effect in 2021.

Its successor starts January 1, 2027. The tax office reports that data collection began in May 2025, that notices will be mailed in late winter or early spring 2027, and that the county holds about 14,736 parcels in the revaluation update. Its presentation shows what changed on individual sales since 2021. One Sparta single-family house from 1968, assessed at $94,100 in 2021, sold in May 2025 for $226,420, which the county lists as a 141 percent increase. Those are single examples, and the county says values moved by different amounts in different areas.

Fire district rates, per $100 of value as printed:

  • Cherry Lane: .04
  • Laurel Springs: .07
  • Sparta: .03
  • Glade Creek: .07
  • Piney Creek: .06

Is there an early-payment discount in Alleghany County?

Yes. Current-year taxes paid between August 1 and August 31 earn a 2 percent discount. Bills left past January 5 pick up 2 percent interest on January 6, plus 0.75 percent at the start of each later month.

Property and improvements must be listed by January 31. The county tax office also handles the exclusions and exemptions the state offers: religious, educational, charitable, elderly or disabled, disabled veteran and farm present use value. For the age-65 or disabled exclusion, 2026 income may not exceed $38,800. Disabled veterans can exclude the first $45,000 of value with no age or income test.

File with the county assessor; the state accepts forms through June 1. If you sell a house that carries one of these programs, tell the buyer's attorney, since the circuit breaker deferral can bring back up to three years of deferred tax when the property is transferred.

How should an Alleghany County owner prepare before closing?

Start with the tax certification, then confirm the deed details and the money. A short order of operations keeps the recording on schedule.

  • Call the tax office at 336-372-8291 for the certification form and the amount owed on the parcel.
  • Check that the deed names the drafter and gives the buyer's mailing address on page one.
  • Arrange for the excise tax and recording fee to be paid at closing, before the 4:30 p.m. recording cutoff.
  • Ask the Clerk of Court at 336-372-3900 how to look up judgments or mechanics liens that could attach to the land.
  • Order a certified copy of the recorded deed afterward if the buyer's lender needs one.

Sellers with a house that needs repairs, liens or inherited title questions can still sell as-is. Recording works the same way for every house; the payoff amounts are what differ.

More questions about Alleghany County, NC Register of Deeds

What time does the Alleghany County Register of Deeds stop accepting documents?

Its cutoff is 4:30 p.m. every day, though the building stays open until 5:00 p.m. Find it at 348 South Main Street in Sparta, phone 336-372-4342.

Is a tax certification required for an Alleghany deed?

Yes. The county says a tax certification form must accompany all deeds. Get it from the Alleghany County Tax Office at 336-372-8291, and expect any unpaid property tax on the parcel to be settled first.

Who owes the deed stamp tax on an Alleghany sale?

The seller, as grantor. The county prints $2.00 per $1,000 of price, paid at recording, which equals the one dollar per $500 in state law.

What does a copy of a recorded Alleghany deed cost?

An in-person plain copy is $.05 a page, and mail requests work too. Certified copies are priced by statute at $5.00 for the opening page and $2.00 for every further page.

When does the next Alleghany County revaluation take effect?

January 1, 2027. Notices of new values are due to be mailed in late winter or early spring 2027, and owners can contest a value before the county appeal board. The prior reset was in 2021.

How do I get a deed into the Avery County records?

Deeds reach the Avery County registry three ways: at the counter, through the mail, or by electronic recording. The counter is staffed Monday to Friday from 8 a.m. until 4:30 in the afternoon, but the last filing of the day is taken at 4:15.

Land records for all 247 square miles of the county sit here, and a public search website shows index entries and document images. Staff only record. Because North Carolina bars them from practicing law, they will not hand out legal forms, coach you on drafting, or comment on what a filed paper does to title; a closing attorney does.

The county tax office adds a useful reminder on its own page: the legal description of a parcel comes from the recorded deed, and the tax maps are meant for valuation only. If the map and the deed disagree, the deed controls.

What fees does the Avery registry charge?

The office's schedule sets a general instrument at $26.00 through 15 pages, and a deed of trust at $64.00 through 35 pages, with $4.00 for each extra page of either. Sale excise tax is separate.

Avery County Register of Deeds fee schedule, as the office prints it (G.S. 161-10)
Document or serviceFee
Deed or other general instrument$26.00 up to 15 pages, plus $4.00 per extra page
Deed of trust$64.00 up to 35 pages, plus $4.00 per extra page
Plat$21.00 per page, 18 by 24 inch only
Excise tax$1 per $500 of the price
Satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trustNo fee
Certified copy$5.00 opening page, $2.00 per following page
Nonstandard document$25.00 extra

Two smaller charges are easy to miss. A document that names more than 20 distinct parties to be indexed adds $2.00 for each name past the twentieth, and a later instrument that refers to more than one earlier recorded instrument costs $25.00 for each additional reference.

Who pays the excise tax when an Avery County house sells?

The seller pays it. G.S. 105-228.30 assigns it to the transferor, who pays the registry first.

The tax is $1 per $500 of price, counting any leftover portion as a full $500. The money is split between county government and the state. Because it follows the contract price, the amount is known as soon as you sign a contract, and it should appear on the settlement statement.

  • Seller: excise tax, plus any recording charge for a release of the old mortgage, which is normally free to record.
  • Buyer: recording fee for the new deed and the lender's deed of trust.
  • Either side: nonstandard document charge if the paperwork does not meet format rules.

A contract can shift costs, so read the settlement statement before signing.

How does recording affect who owns the property?

Under G.S. 47-18 a transfer only binds lien creditors and later buyers once it is registered in the county of the land, and priority runs by recording time.

That is why Avery County closings end with a recording and not just a signing. A deed that sits unrecorded in a drawer leaves the buyer exposed. The register's office also holds the paperwork that clears the seller's side, such as the satisfaction of a prior deed of trust, so a payoff letter and a recorded cancellation should both show up in the index.

Keep the recorded copy and the recording stamp with your closing file, since they are the proof that the transfer took effect on a given date.

What kind of county is Avery, and who lives in its houses?

Avery County sits high in the northwestern mountains, bordered by Tennessee and by Watauga, Caldwell, Burke and Mitchell counties. Its seat, Newland, stands at 3,589 feet, which the county calls the highest county seat in the eastern United States, and the county straddles the eastern continental divide near 4,000 feet.

The county names Colonel Waightstill Avery of Morganton as its namesake. Winters are real here. The county reports an average of 58 inches of snow and temperatures about ten degrees cooler than Asheville or Charlotte, and the ski slopes stay covered from mid-November through March. Seven towns sit inside the county: Banner Elk, Beech Mountain, Crossnore, Elk Park, Newland, Seven Devils and Sugar Mountain.

Newland began as "Old Fields of Toe", a broad flat valley at the headwaters of the Toe River. The county's tax records divide the land into eight townships (Altamont, Banner Elk, Beech Mountain, Cranberry, Linville, Roaring Creek, Toe River and Wilson's Creek) and ten fire districts. When you ask the tax office for a payoff, give the township or town along with the parcel details so the right rates are applied.

Federal housing and population figures:

  • People: 18,110 as of July 2025.
  • Housing units: 14,597 in 2025 against 6,791 households for 2020 to 2024.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 83.0 percent.
  • Median owner-occupied home value: $265,800.
  • Median gross rent: $773.
  • Residents 65 and over: 26.9 percent.

More than twice as many housing units as households points to a large stock of vacation homes, which is worth keeping in mind when a house has been empty through winters.

How do Avery County taxes reach a closing?

Avery County's tax office bills real and personal property under two divisions, assessment and collections, and its rate page lists a 2025 county rate of 0.335 plus a 0.065 fire rate for a total of 0.40. No unit appears beside the numbers, so have the tax office confirm how they apply to a bill.

The current values date from the January 1, 2022 revaluation, with notices mailed that March. Tax bills follow state timing: due September 1, interest starting after January 5. Avery's listing period runs through January, and the county told owners that taxpayers carry the duty to list even if no form arrives.

The county tax office phone is 828-733-8214 for assessment and 828-733-8228 for collections. Before closing, call both offices and pass the figures to the title attorney.

What checks help an Avery County seller before recording day?

Confirm the pieces below a few days ahead and the recording will go through at the first attempt.

  • Have the deed drafted by an attorney and notarized, with the preparer's name on it.
  • Print on white paper in a legible font with a clear top margin so the nonstandard charge is avoided.
  • Bring a plat only on 18 by 24 inch sheets if a subdivision map is part of the transaction.
  • Plan to reach the register before the 4:15 p.m. recording cutoff.
  • Search the online index for the property to see any recorded easements or old deeds of trust that still show open.

If you hold a house you inherited or one that needs repairs, the same recording steps apply. Sellers who want a quick, as-is sale still go through the same register, and the same tax and excise tax charges follow the contract price.

More questions about Avery County, NC Register of Deeds

When can I record in Avery County?

Weekdays the office keeps 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. hours, and filings are accepted until 4:15 p.m. Counter, mail and electronic submissions are all taken.

What will Avery County charge me to record my deed?

A general instrument is $26.00 through page 15 and $4.00 for each page beyond. Excise tax is extra at $1 per $500, and a nonstandard paper adds $25.00.

Is there a fee to record the release of a mortgage in Avery County?

No. The register's schedule lists satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust as no fee, which matches the statewide fee statute.

Can the Avery County register of deeds give legal advice about my deed?

No. Staff cannot practice law, so they will not supply forms, show you how to fill one in, or explain its effect. An attorney can.

Who gives me a tax payoff figure in Avery County?

Call the Avery County tax office. Dial 828-733-8214 for assessment or 828-733-8228 for collections. Request this year's balance and any earlier balance for the parcel.

How do I reach the Beaufort County registry?

Walk in at 112 W 2nd Street, Washington, NC 27889, or write to P.O. Box 514. Staff keep weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., stop taking filings at 4:45 p.m., and answer at 252-946-2323.

The county page cites G.S. 84-4 and 84-5 to explain that staff cannot help prepare legal papers. Arrive with a finished deed from your lawyer.

What must a Beaufort deed show on its face?

The office's recording guide mixes state standards with local steps.

  • Letter or legal paper, printed on one side in legible type of 9 points or larger on white stock.
  • Three blank inches at the head of page one, and half-inch margins elsewhere.
  • The kind of instrument written at the top of the first page.
  • A preparer's name on every deed and deed of trust.
  • On a deed, the buyer's address plus a note on whether the seller lived there as a primary residence.
  • A sign-off from Land Records on deeds and certain maps before filing.

Paper that misses the format rules can still be filed, subject to a $25.00 nonstandard fee, and the register may waive that fee when only the type size is short and the text is legible. Surveys and plats, along with Torrens documents, are not accepted electronically, so they go in on paper.

Why does a Beaufort County deed go through Land Records first?

The county ties its mapping and tax listing to recorded deeds, so Land Records looks at a deed before the register files it. That office is at 220 N. Market Street in Washington and the phone is 252-946-6591.

Land Records manages the county's parcel mapping and GIS databases, applies recorded documents such as wills and deeds when it administers tax listings, and helps the public and professionals with record reviews. For a seller, the takeaway is to drop the deed there early, because the register's guide puts that approval ahead of recording.

Beaufort also posts a resolution on tax certification for deeds among the register's downloads. Ask the register or the tax collector whether a certificate is needed for your closing, because that rule is set locally.

What are the costs to record in Beaufort County?

State law in G.S. 161-10 fixes most amounts, and the county posts its own schedule file. The table pairs those amounts with the nonstandard charge from the office guide.

Recording charges that apply in Beaufort County (state statute G.S. 161-10 and the register's recording guide)
ItemCharge
General instrument, such as a deed$26.00 up to 15 pages, then $4.00 a page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 up to 35 pages, then $4.00 a page
Release of a deed of trustNo fee
Plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 for the first sheet, $2.00 for each more
Nonstandard document$25.00

Excise tax is a separate line: the seller pays a dollar per $500 of price at the registry, and the county retains half. For anything out of the ordinary, request the office's current schedule.

How does the Beaufort County fraud alert protect owners?

Beaufort's registry emails you, at no charge, when a recorded document matches a name you enroll. Each email address can list five names, and only filings made after signup count.

The office explains the reason for the service plainly: it must record any document that is properly executed and presented with payment, and it cannot know whether a signature is forged. Nothing can be removed from the official records after recording, even if a document is proven fraudulent. An owner who suspects fraud should call the sheriff's office at 252-946-7111 and speak to an attorney, because the register has no power to reverse the filing.

A name you enroll can be your own or a relative's, which suits owners of land they rarely visit.

What is Beaufort County like for a seller?

Beaufort County is a coastal plain county built around the Pamlico River, with 88,000 acres of water and a long border on the Pamlico Sound. Washington, the county seat, sits where the Tar and Pamlico rivers meet.

The county was formed in 1705 as Pamptecough Precinct and named in 1712. Bath, founded in 1705, is the oldest town in the state. Seven municipalities lie within it: Aurora, Bath, Belhaven, Chocowinity, Pantego, Washington and Washington Park. Washington once had a busy port and a thriving shipbuilding trade and remains the cultural and economic center, Chocowinity served as a Norfolk Southern railroad hub from 1910, and the waterfronts that used to ship lumber and naval stores have turned more recreational and residential. Census figures:

  • Population: 44,670 in 2025, down from 47,759 at the 2010 census.
  • Land area: 832.74 square miles.
  • Housing units: 25,204 in 2025, with 19,385 households.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 69.5 percent.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $192,700.
  • Median gross rent: $871.
  • Residents 65 and older: 29.1 percent; veterans: 3,361.

Waterfront and inland parcels do not move together. The county itself notes that property on or near the water has historically changed in value much faster than inland land.

How do Beaufort County taxes interact with a sale?

Bills are issued as of July 1 and fall due September 1, with interest and enforced collection starting if payment is not in by January 5. For real estate, the owner on January 1 is the listing taxpayer and remains responsible until the past due date, whatever the buyer and seller agree at closing.

That is a real trap for a seller. A seller who closes after the bills go out may still get one in the mail, and the county asks that it be sent on to the buyer or returned to the collector. Escrow lenders are not automatic either: the owner must tell the lender the amount and confirm with the collector that payment arrived.

The 2025 revaluation took effect January 1, 2025, and the commissioners set a six-year cycle going forward. Value appeals may be filed from January each year, up to the adjournment of the county review board, typically in mid-April. The county commissioners set county, fire and EMS district rates when the budget is adopted, while town officials set municipal rates. Vehicles are taxed through the NCDMV at tag renewal, not on the real estate bill. The tax collector offers payment plans with a 20 percent down payment, set up in person between January 6 and June 30.

More questions about Beaufort County, NC Register of Deeds

When is the last filing time in Beaufort County?

Filing closes at 4:45 p.m., fifteen minutes before the 5 p.m. weekday close. The office is at 112 W 2nd Street in Washington and can be reached at 252-946-2323.

Does a deed need Land Records approval in Beaufort County?

Yes. The register's recording guide says deeds and some maps must be approved by the Beaufort County Land Records office before recording. Land Records is at 220 N. Market Street, phone 252-946-6591.

Can I record a plat electronically in Beaufort County?

No. The county lists survey maps and plats, along with Torrens documents, as not accepted electronically. Those two are the only document types the county page excludes from electronic recording.

Who pays the tax bill after a Beaufort sale?

The January 1 owner stays responsible until the past due date, regardless of what the buyer and seller arranged at closing, according to the county. Send any notice to the buyer or back to the collector.

Can Beaufort County warn me about filings in my name?

Yes. The register runs a free fraud alert email service. You can enroll five names per email address and receive a notice when a matching document is recorded, but only for documents recorded after signup.

Where is the Cumberland County Register of Deeds and how do I reach it?

The office sits in Room 114 of the Judge E. Maurice Braswell Cumberland County Courthouse, 117 Dick Street in Fayetteville, and the land records line is 910-678-7775. The office keeps its own website at ccrod.org, where the posted office hours and the yearly holiday schedule live.

Cumberland County's land records reach back to 1754, which the office describes as the official start of the county. Other business at the same counter includes notary oaths and vital records, and retired service members can file discharge papers (DD-214) free of charge.

Why does the filing time on a Fayetteville-area deed matter?

North Carolina gives a buyer no shield against competing claimants until the deed reaches the public record at the local courthouse. When two instruments compete, whichever was registered first generally wins, so the time stamp carries real weight.

A few habits keep a sale clean:

  • Get every signature notarized before the paperwork goes to Dick Street.
  • Pair the deed with payment of both tax and fee.
  • Ask your closing attorney to tell you the exact filing date and time.
  • Save the book and page reference from the recorded copy.

Counter staff will not draft or advise on deeds, so wording questions belong with an attorney.

Which recording charges does the Cumberland County office collect?

The posted schedule dates from October 1, 2016. Filing an ordinary deed starts at $26.00, and a mortgage filing starts at $64.00. The table lists the rest of what the office prints.

Checks and money orders go out in the office's name, and a re-recording is billed like the original filing.

How is the Cumberland County deed excise tax figured?

The county's recording page states the tax as $2.00 against each $1,000 of price, with any leftover fraction counted as a full unit. The statute words the same rate as $1.00 against each $500. Payment travels with the filing fee, and the figure appears on page one of the deed.

The statute's "transferor," meaning the seller, owes it, and the office collects before it records anything. Revenue is then shared evenly between the county and the state. If the contract price falls between round numbers, have your closing attorney supply the exact amount instead of guessing at the window.

What must a deed show before the Cumberland County office will accept it?

Page one of a North Carolina deed must name whoever drafted it, and it should also give a return address. The office lists these points on its recording requirements page:

  • The draftsman line, usually written "Prepared by" or "Drawn by."
  • A return address block, also on page one.
  • The excise tax or revenue amount on the front of the deed.
  • Paper size, margins, font size and page limits that meet state recording standards.
  • Notarization of the signatures before filing.

Satisfactions and UCC filings are exempt from the formatting rules. A deed that misses the mark is still accepted, with $25.00 added for non-standard format.

How does the Property Notification service protect a Cumberland County owner?

This is a no-cost email alert sent whenever a recorded document lists your name. The office pitches it as a defense against deed fraud and tells owners who see an unauthorized filing to call a real estate attorney.

To enroll, visit ccrod.org, pick Records Search, choose New Property Notification and follow the screens. Each alert lists the name matched, the date, the book and page, and a link to the document. The office says plainly that the alerts are no guarantee against fraud. Owners of a vacant or inherited Fayetteville property may find the alerts useful while the house is empty.

How do Cumberland County deed records tie into the property tax listing?

Tax Administration decides who the listing owner is by reading instruments indexed at the Register of Deeds and at the Clerk of Court's estates division on January 1. The county keeps a permanent listing, so owners report only what changed, such as a deck, an in-ground pool or a remodel. Forms are requested back by January 31.

Send them to Tax Administration, Attn: Real Estate Division, P.O. Box 449, Fayetteville, NC 28302, or drop them at Room 530 of the courthouse. Statewide, the bill is due September 1, interest starts January 6 at two percent, with three-quarters of a percent added for each month from February 1 on. Ask Tax Administration how a mid-year sale is handled on the current bill.

A veteran with a permanent, total, service-connected disability rating may apply to the county assessor for the state exclusion, which removes $45,000 from the appraised value.

How does Cumberland County's housing stock look in the Census data?

The Census Bureau puts Cumberland County at 338,473 people in mid-2025, spread over 146,623 housing units and 652.56 square miles of land. Owners occupy 55.0 percent of the homes counted for 2020 to 2024.

  • Median gross rent is $1,222 a month.
  • The county counts 129,758 households averaging 2.48 people.
  • Veterans number 40,226.
  • Median household income is $61,291, in 2024 dollars.

These QuickFacts numbers cover the whole county and say little about a single street.

What should a Cumberland County seller check ahead of signing?

Begin with the mortgage. Filing a satisfaction of a paid-off loan costs nothing, so a cleared mortgage should end with that document on record. If payments have lapsed, the lender uses a power-of-sale case heard by the clerk of superior court, and once a sale is reported anyone may file an upset bid within ten days, at least five percent above the price and no less than $750.00 higher.

Next, study the title. Pull the last recorded deed, look for liens, and check whether a deed of trust remains open. A house that came through an estate also warrants a look at the clerk's estates division records. A sale that skips repairs may trim the to-do list, though the deed, excise tax and filing fee are still due.

Who pays the deed excise tax when selling a house in Cumberland County?

The seller pays, and the statute calls that party the transferor. It is handed over at the counter before the deed is filed. The county page prints $2.00 against each $1,000 of price, and the statute prints $1.00 against each $500.

Mail it to Tax Administration, Attn: Real Estate Division, P.O. Box 449, Fayetteville, NC 28302, or bring it to Room 530 of the courthouse. The county asks for forms by January 31 so changes reach that year's assessment.

Sellers who want certainty can ask that the tax collector be paid directly out of closing funds. The tax collector's phone number is 336-242-2180, and the same office handles the tax certifications the Register of Deeds requires. Because a certificate and a recorded deed depend on each other, a seller who clears the tax account first usually avoids a delay at the recording counter.

How big is the Davidson County housing market?

Census estimates for mid-2025 show 180,182 residents, a rise of 6.7 percent since the spring 2020 base, living among 79,412 housing units. The county covers 553.18 square miles, and owners live in 74.4 percent of occupied homes.

  • Home value at the Census median: $219,100.
  • Rent at the median: $901 gross.
  • Monthly cost for owners with a mortgage: $1,355 at the median.
  • Households: 69,846, averaging 2.45 people.
  • Persons 65 and over: 20.8 percent.
  • Permits pulled for new building in 2025: 1,216.

Few people move in a given year, with 92.2 percent in their prior-year home. Those figures describe the whole county, not a single town.

What other records does the Davidson County office handle?

Beyond deeds, the office takes military discharges and assumed business name filings by mail at P.O. Box 464, and sellers who are heirs often need its vital records too. Marriage license applications are online, and the applicant then calls to schedule an appointment. A marriage license is valid for 60 days only.

Funeral homes with escrow accounts send certificate requests by fax, and orders are mailed within 48 hours. Others bring the request with payment and proof of their funeral home status, or mail it with a stamped return envelope. Heirs selling a parent's house usually need a death certificate for the estate file, so ordering a few early saves a second trip.

What should a Davidson County seller do before the deed goes in?

Work through a short list in order:

  • Pull the tax bill for the parcel and see whether anything is delinquent.
  • Decide whether an attorney will close the sale or you will request a tax certificate yourself.
  • Confirm the draftsman line and return address on the deed.
  • Arrange payment of the excise tax and filing fee for the same day.
  • Get the loan payoff and a recorded release of the deed of trust.

If the loan is in default, power-of-sale foreclosure is heard before the clerk of superior court, with ten days to file an upset bid after a sale report. Request a written payoff statement from the lender early.

More questions about Davidson County, NC Register of Deeds

What time does the Davidson County Register of Deeds stop recording?

Recording stops at 4:30pm sharp, even though the office stays open until 5pm Monday through Friday. The county put that rule in place on August 1, 2020.

Why was my Davidson County deed refused for taxes?

Since March 1, 2019, the office accepts a real property deed only with a Tax Administrator certificate showing no delinquent taxes, or under a closing attorney who agrees to pay any delinquent taxes from the proceeds. The certificate can take up to two business days.

How far back do the online Davidson County land records go?

Records are indexed from 1984 to the present. For earlier records, contact the Register of Deeds office at 336-242-2150.

Who pays the excise tax on a Davidson County deed?

The seller does, at the counter, ahead of filing. The statute's rate is one dollar for each $500 of price or part of $500.

Can I record documents by mail in Davidson County?

Military discharges and assumed business name filings can be mailed to P.O. Box 464, Lexington, NC 27293. The assumed business name fee is $26.00, and a stamped return envelope is needed for return.
